newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH EUROTEL 1996 PROFIT DIPS AS INVESTMENT RISES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH EUROTEL 1996 PROFIT DIPS AS INVESTMENT RISES.

text.p: Czech mobile phone operator Eurotel, a joint-venture of SPT Telecom a.s. and U.S. firms Bell Atlantic International and U.S. West Media Group, on Thursday said its 1996 net profit eased to 435 million crowns.
Eurotel's revenues nearly doubled to 4.64 billion crowns in 1996 from 2.98 billion the previous, as the company closed the year with a 79 percent market share.
But company officials said its 1996 net result was down from 566 million crowns in 1995 because of heavier investment -- which rose 1.73 billion crowns to 2.65 billion -- and rising operating costs.
Eurotel, which launched an NMT analogue network earlier this decade, invested heavily into the development of its Global System for Mobile (GSM) network, which began operation in July of last year.
"The increase in revenues corresponds to the dynamics of the market which was higher than we expected," Eurotel chief financial operator Michal Herman told a news conference.
Eurotel said that as of April 1997, it had just over 204,000 customers, 139,577 of which are registered to its GSM network.
The U.S. consortium holds a 49 percent stake in Eurotel, while SPT Telecom holds a 51 percent stake.
